facts.fact_text: On 4 September 2003 a few dozen residents gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square.
The applicant was among the residents who gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
The police dispersed the crowd at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003 by force.
According to the administrative-arrest record of 4 September 2003, the applicant was arrested for refusing to comply with a lawful order of the police.

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to serve written notice on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (§ 2).
Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (§ 3).

Under Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens.

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body could refuse to accept the notice if the purpose of the assembly was contrary to the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, generally accepted public morals, if there was no undertaking on the part of the organisers to ensure public safety, if the assembly coincided in time and place with another one, if it threatened normal functioning of companies or organisations, or if it required suspending public or rail transport (§ 4).
The Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998) was in force at the material time.

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), the Ministry of the Interior fought terrorism by way of preventing, detecting and putting an end to terrorist offences pursuing lucrative goals (section 7 § 3).

Under the Suppression of Terrorism Act (Federal Law no. 130-FZ of 25 July 1998), regional executive bodies, municipal bodies, public associations and organisations and State officials were required to assist the authorities responsible for suppression of terrorism (section 9 § 1).

Under Article 27.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, administrative arrest — a temporary restriction of liberty of an individual — may be ordered in exceptional circumstances where it is necessary for a correct and prompt examination of the administrative case.

Under Article 27.5 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, the duration of administrative arrest must not exceed three hours, except for situations described in paragraphs 2 and 3 of that Article.

Under Article 27.5 § 3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, anyone who is subject to administrative proceedings concerning an offence punishable by administrative detention may be placed under administrative arrest for a period not exceeding forty-eight hours.
